title: Automotive apprentice starter toolkit
summary: Build the starter kit in stages.
body: Begin with the current school or employer list, then mark the tools already owned and any equipment the shop supplies. Buy core drivers, pliers and sockets before optional power or premium diagnostic upgrades.
caution: Check SAE coverage, exact spark-plug sizes, the required feeler-gauge range, hammers, precision rules and fender protection separately. This directory is not a complete school compliance list.

title: Vehicle diagnostics buying plan
summary: Define the required diagnostic function first.
body: Record the vehicle and symptom, confirm the required system access, then check exact tool coverage before ordering. Read codes and live data in the context of service information; clear codes only when the diagnostic procedure calls for it.
caution: Enhanced system access and bidirectional functions vary by vehicle. Include updates, gateway access, adapters and training in the purchase decision.

title: Battery and no-start electrical diagnosis
summary: Separate battery condition from the circuit fault.
body: Inspect the supported low-voltage battery and connections, assess battery/starting/charging behaviour with appropriate equipment, and use a meter when the fault requires circuit measurements. Choose charging or starting support for its intended role.
caution: This is an equipment plan for documented conventional low-voltage applications, not instructions for EV high-voltage work. Match chemistry and ratings to every connected device.

title: Wheel removal and refitting equipment plan
summary: Plan support, removal and final tightening together.
body: Check approved lifting points and surface conditions, select suitable lifting and support equipment, then match sockets and access tools to the fasteners. Include an appropriate calibrated torque wrench for the vehicle’s final tightening specification.
caution: A floor jack is not working support. An impact setting does not establish final wheel torque. Check pressure against the vehicle cold-pressure specification after the relevant service checks.

title: Brake service toolkit
summary: Identify the brake design before choosing retraction tools.
body: Start with the vehicle service procedure and inspect the actual brake arrangement. Measuring pads, retracting pistons and bleeding hydraulics require different tools; buy only the supported method and adapters.
caution: Some rear and EPB systems require a different retraction procedure, while ABS bleeding can require supported scan-tool functions. Do not treat a generic piston compressor or pressure bleeder as universal.

title: Routine servicing and oil-change toolkit
summary: Match access, filter geometry and fluid handling.
body: Confirm the engine’s filter and drain arrangement, plan safe access and capture capacity, and select the correct removal or cap tool. Keep the clean filling container separate from used-fluid capture.
caution: Use the specified fluid, quantity, installation method and tightening requirements. The equipment list does not replace the vehicle procedure, temperature precautions or suitable disposal.

title: Workshop and mobile-mechanic setup
summary: Build around the workspace and the tools already available.
body: Plan lighting, storage, power, compressed air and suitable working surfaces together. A mobile kit needs secure transport and a realistic carrying weight; a workshop may already supply much of the shared equipment.
caution: Choose optional upgrades for recurring work rather than collecting every listed product. Keep hazardous tasks, PPE and lifting/support requirements specific to the workspace and vehicles.
